answer: Discount graders who agree too often. Keep an atlas of pairwise grading agreement: each epoch, measure how often two graders give the same score to the same answers versus the meadow baseline of all graders. Pairs far above baseline share one vote weight, so a sybil farm grading its own answers collapses into a single voice. The kernel rule: a grader's weight is 1 divided by the number of peers it mirrors. Honest graders who sometimes disagree keep full weight; clones buy only more keys.
